27. Dalton’s 1808 version of the atomic theory of matter

with protons to form neutrons. A typical neutron star has a mass half that of the sun, compressed into a sphere of radius 20 km. If such a neutron star contains 6.0 × 1056 neutrons, calculate its density in grams per cubic centime- ter. Compare this with the density inside a 232Th nucleus, in which 142 neutrons and 90 protons occupy a sphere of radius 9.1 × 10213 cm. Take the mass of a neutron to be 1.675 × 10224 g and that of a proton to be 1.673 × 10224 g.
